DNS Security Scan: cloudflare.com
========================================
Overall Score: 95/100 (A+)
1 high-severity issue(s) found. Grade: A+

Email Security Maturity: Stage 4 — Hardened
Comprehensive email and DNS security posture with defense in depth.

Scoring Profile: mail_enabled (MX present, DKIM present, BIMI present, DMARC enforcing, SSL valid, CAA present)

Category Scores:
------------------------------
  ✓ SPF        85/100
  ✓ DMARC      90/100
  ⚠ DKIM       70/100
  ✓ DNSSEC     100/100
  ✓ SSL        95/100
  ⚠ MTA_STS    75/100
  ✓ NS         95/100
  ✓ CAA        100/100
  ✓ BIMI       95/100
  ✓ TLSRPT     100/100
  ✓ SUBDOMAIN_TAKEOVER 100/100

  ✓ DANE       80/100
  ✓ MX         100/100
  ✓ DANE_HTTPS 95/100
  ✓ SVCB_HTTPS 100/100
  ✓ SUBDOMAILING 100/100
  ✓ DNSKEY_STRENGTH 100/100
  ✓ PTR        100/100

Findings:
------------------------------
  [MEDIUM] TXT RRset exceeds UDP limit
    The combined TXT RRset for cloudflare.com is ~2438 bytes, which exceeds the 512-byte UDP limit and requires TCP fallback. Legacy resolvers and restrictive middleboxes that do not retry over TCP may only see the first ~512 bytes, silently...
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: Some receivers may not see the full SPF record, producing inconsistent authentication results.
    Adverse Consequences: Mail can fail authentication at a subset of receivers in a way that is hard to reproduce or diagnose.
  [LOW] No forensic reporting configured (ruf= absent)
    Aggregate reporting (rua=) is configured but forensic reporting (ruf=) is not. Forensic reports provide detailed failure information useful for troubleshooting.
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: There is no visibility into authentication results or spoofing attempts against the domain.
    Adverse Consequences: Tightening the policy becomes risky because legitimate senders cannot be identified first, and abuse of the domain goes unnoticed.
  [LOW] Relaxed DKIM alignment
    DKIM alignment mode is relaxed (adkim=r or unset). Consider adkim=s (strict) for stronger authentication.
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: Alignment is looser or reporting is less complete than the strictest posture.
    Adverse Consequences: Borderline spoofing techniques may pass alignment and some diagnostic detail is unavailable.
  [MEDIUM] Legacy RSA key: smtpapi
    DKIM RSA key for "smtpapi" is legacy (1024 bits). RFC 8301 §3.2 requires at least 1024-bit RSA and recommends at least 2048 bits. Plan an upgrade to 2048-bit RSA or Ed25519 where supported; if your mail provider manages this key, ask abo...
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: The authenticity guarantee DKIM provides for this selector is weaker than intended.
    Adverse Consequences: A forged but validly-signed message would pass DKIM and DMARC, making impersonation highly credible.
  [MEDIUM] Missing DKIM version tag: smtpapi
    DKIM selector "smtpapi" is missing the v= tag. Should be set to v=DKIM1.
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: Signature verification for this selector is unreliable across receivers.
    Adverse Consequences: Legitimate signed mail may fail DKIM at some receivers with no consistent pattern.
  [LOW] HSTS max-age too short
    HSTS max-age is 15780000 seconds (183 days). Recommended minimum is 31536000 (1 year).
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: Partial HSTS coverage leaves windows where transport security guarantees are weaker than expected.
    Adverse Consequences: Subdomains or returning sessions may still face avoidable downgrade exposure and policy non-compliance findings.
  [HIGH] MTA-STS policy file not accessible
    MTA-STS policy file at https://mta-sts.cloudflare.com/.well-known/mta-sts.txt returned HTTP 530. The policy file must be accessible over HTTPS.
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: Inbound mail is not protected against TLS downgrade despite MTA-STS appearing to be configured.
    Adverse Consequences: Message content can be intercepted on a downgraded connection while the domain believes STS is enforcing.
  [LOW] Low nameserver diversity
    All nameservers are under cloudflare.com. Cloudflare's anycast network provides built-in geographic redundancy, so this is lower risk than single-provider setups on traditional DNS hosts. For maximum independence, a secondary DNS provide...
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: DNS resilience and consistency are reduced, increasing partial or full resolution outage risk.
    Adverse Consequences: Availability incidents can affect websites, APIs, and transactional workflows.
  [LOW] BIMI logo exceeds 32 KB
    BIMI logo exceeds 32 KB. The BIMI specification recommends logos be under 32 KB for reliable display in email clients.
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: BIMI works but is not at its most complete configuration.
    Adverse Consequences: Minor reduction in display coverage across providers. Note that BIMI is a brand-presentation control: there is no controlled evidence that it reduces phishing susceptibility, and a verified logo renders on any message that passes DMARC for the domain — including mail sent from a compromised mailbox. Weigh the mark-certificate cost against that, and keep BIMI as a brand-presentation investment rather than an anti-phishing one.
  [MEDIUM] CSP allows unsafe-inline scripts
    Content-Security-Policy contains 'unsafe-inline' in the script source, which undermines XSS protection. Use nonces or hashes instead.
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: This issue weakens defenses and compounds risk when paired with other gaps.
    Adverse Consequences: Over time it can degrade reliability, security assurance, and compliance posture.
  [MEDIUM] CSP allows unsafe-eval
    Content-Security-Policy contains 'unsafe-eval' in the script source, allowing dynamic code execution. This weakens XSS protection.
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: This issue weakens defenses and compounds risk when paired with other gaps.
    Adverse Consequences: Over time it can degrade reliability, security assurance, and compliance posture.
  [LOW] DANE TLSA configured for _25._tcp.mxa-canary.global.inbound.cf-emailsecurity.net
    11 DANE TLSA records present and syntactically well-formed for _25._tcp.mxa-canary.global.inbound.cf-emailsecurity.net. This check does not verify the pinned data against the certificate the server presents, so a stale pin is not detecte...
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: DANE protection is effective but not at its strongest, widely-interoperable configuration.
    Adverse Consequences: Minor reduction in the robustness of certificate pinning.
  [LOW] DANE TLSA configured for _25._tcp.mxb-canary.global.inbound.cf-emailsecurity.net
    2 DANE TLSA records present and syntactically well-formed for _25._tcp.mxb-canary.global.inbound.cf-emailsecurity.net. This check does not verify the pinned data against the certificate the server presents, so a stale pin is not detected...
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: DANE protection is effective but not at its strongest, widely-interoperable configuration.
    Adverse Consequences: Minor reduction in the robustness of certificate pinning.
  [LOW] DANE TLSA configured for _25._tcp.mxa.global.inbound.cf-emailsecurity.net
    11 DANE TLSA records present and syntactically well-formed for _25._tcp.mxa.global.inbound.cf-emailsecurity.net. This check does not verify the pinned data against the certificate the server presents, so a stale pin is not detected here....
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: DANE protection is effective but not at its strongest, widely-interoperable configuration.
    Adverse Consequences: Minor reduction in the robustness of certificate pinning.
  [LOW] DANE TLSA configured for _25._tcp.mxb.global.inbound.cf-emailsecurity.net
    11 DANE TLSA records present and syntactically well-formed for _25._tcp.mxb.global.inbound.cf-emailsecurity.net. This check does not verify the pinned data against the certificate the server presents, so a stale pin is not detected here....
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: DANE protection is effective but not at its strongest, widely-interoperable configuration.
    Adverse Consequences: Minor reduction in the robustness of certificate pinning.
  [LOW] No DANE TLSA for HTTPS
    No TLSA record found at _443._tcp.cloudflare.com. DANE can pin web server certificates to DNS, providing an additional layer of trust beyond the CA system. Implement DANE-EE (usage 3) with DNSSEC enabled for maximum security.
    Confidence: deterministic
    Potential Impact: HTTPS certificate pinning via DANE is absent or misconfigured, leaving TLS trust dependent solely on the CA system.
    Adverse Consequences: A rogue or compromised CA can issue a fraudulent certificate, enabling undetected MITM attacks.

findings.title: TXT RRset exceeds UDP limit
findings.detail: The combined TXT RRset for cloudflare.com is ~2438 bytes, which exceeds the 512-byte UDP limit and requires TCP fallback. Legacy resolvers and restrictive middleboxes that do not retry over TCP may only see the first ~512 bytes, silently breaking SPF for some receiving MTAs. RFC 7208 §3.4 advises keeping the SPF record and surrounding TXT RRset small enough to fit a single UDP packet.

findings.title: Relaxed SPF alignment
findings.detail: SPF alignment mode is relaxed (aspf=r or unset). Strict alignment (aspf=s) only strengthens DMARC when every authorized sender's return-path (envelope-from) domain exactly matches the From domain — untrue for most ESP-relayed mail (e.g. Resend, SendGrid, Mailchimp, SES with a custom MAIL FROM), where the return-path sits on a subdomain: wherever the From domain differs from it (typically the apex), aspf=s fails SPF alignment for that traffic and leaves DKIM as the only authentication leg. Mail whose From address stays on that same subdomain still aligns under aspf=s. Set aspf=s only after DMARC aggregate reports confirm every sender's return-path domain exactly matches the From domain; otherwise aspf=r is the correct setting.

findings.title: Low nameserver diversity
findings.detail: All nameservers are under cloudflare.com. Cloudflare's anycast network provides built-in geographic redundancy, so this is lower risk than single-provider setups on traditional DNS hosts. For maximum independence, a secondary DNS provider can be added.

findings.title: CAA properly configured
findings.detail: CAA records found with issue, issuewild, and iodef tags configured.

findings.title: CAA policy is DNSSEC-protected
findings.detail: The CAA RRset at cloudflare.com was returned DNSSEC-authenticated. Under CA/Browser Forum TLS BR §4.2.2 subsection 1.3 (in force 2026-03-15) CAs must validate CAA lookups with DNSSEC to the root and must not treat validation errors as permission to issue, so this policy is cryptographically enforceable rather than advisory — it cannot be stripped in transit to unlock issuance.

findings.title: BIMI authority evidence present
findings.detail: BIMI record includes a mark certificate reference (a= authority evidence): https://www.cloudflare.com/cloudflare_1171114652.pem. The certificate type is not determined from the URL alone.

findings.title: BIMI logo exceeds 32 KB
findings.detail: BIMI logo exceeds 32 KB. The BIMI specification recommends logos be under 32 KB for reliable display in email clients.

findings.title: TLS-RPT record configured
findings.detail: TLS-RPT record found and configured at _smtp._tls.cloudflare.com: v=TLSRPTv1; rua=mailto:rua@cloudflare.com;

findings.title: No dangling CNAME records found
findings.detail: No subdomain takeover vectors detected for cloudflare.com among known/active subdomains.

findings.title: CSP allows unsafe-inline scripts
findings.detail: Content-Security-Policy contains 'unsafe-inline' in the script source, which undermines XSS protection. Use nonces or hashes instead.

findings.title: CSP allows unsafe-eval
findings.detail: Content-Security-Policy contains 'unsafe-eval' in the script source, allowing dynamic code execution. This weakens XSS protection.

findings.title: No COEP header
findings.detail: No Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy header found. COEP, combined with COOP, enables cross-origin isolation and mitigates Spectre-class side-channel attacks.

findings.title: HTTP origin attributed to Cloudflare CDN (heuristic)
findings.detail: Cloudflare CDN inferred from the origin ASN (AS13335) of the resolved A-record IP via team-cymru. Header-based CDN detection was inconclusive — this CDN does not emit a vendor-specific response header, and the scanner runs inside a Cloudflare Worker, which rewrites server: cloudflare on every outbound response.

findings.title: DANE TLSA configured for _25._tcp.mxa-canary.global.inbound.cf-emailsecurity.net
findings.detail: 11 DANE TLSA records present and syntactically well-formed for _25._tcp.mxa-canary.global.inbound.cf-emailsecurity.net. This check does not verify the pinned data against the certificate the server presents, so a stale pin is not detected here. Authentication succeeds while any one association still matches, so a single superseded record during a rollover is not itself fatal; where the RRset is DNSSEC-authenticated and none match, DANE-validating clients reject the connection. Confirm each pin matches the live certificate after every certificate rotation.

findings.detail: 4 mail exchange record(s) present.

findings.title: No DANE TLSA for HTTPS
findings.detail: No TLSA record found at _443._tcp.cloudflare.com. DANE can pin web server certificates to DNS, providing an additional layer of trust beyond the CA system. Implement DANE-EE (usage 3) with DNSSEC enabled for maximum security.

findings.title: HTTPS record configured
findings.detail: HTTPS record found at cloudflare.com (priority 1): ALPN= h3, h2 .

findings.title: HTTP/3 (QUIC) advertised via HTTPS record
findings.detail: HTTPS record at cloudflare.com advertises HTTP/3 (h3) ALPN, enabling QUIC-based transport. This provides improved performance and resilience, especially on lossy networks.

findings.title: No SubdoMailing risk detected
findings.detail: Analyzed 6 SPF include/redirect domain(s) for cloudflare.com. All resolve correctly with no takeover indicators.

findings.title: Modern DNSKEY algorithm (ECDSA P-256)
findings.detail: cloudflare.com signs with DNSKEY algorithm 13 (ECDSA P-256), a modern and recommended choice.

findings.title: No reverse DNS (PTR) for mail servers
findings.detail: None of the 4 mail-server IP(s) have a PTR record. mxa-canary.global.inbound.cf-emailsecurity.net (172.65.169.99): no PTR record; mxb-canary.global.inbound.cf-emailsecurity.net (172.65.65.66): no PTR record; mxa.global.inbound.cf-emailsecurity.net (172.65.64.137): no PTR record; mxb.global.inbound.cf-emailsecurity.net (172.65.64.137): no PTR record
